parameters.P4_NOT_EVALUABLE_RULE: P4 at a (class, rate) is — (not evaluable) when the ledger E or a collected sensor family (L, M, S, T) is not at the operating point there; highest_rate names every — rate as '— at {rates}'
parameters.PROBE_TRACE_RULE: TeaStore and OTel: an untokened trace rooted at the entry service whose root starts inside a stamped probe window (the receipt's probes and [revert issued, ready]) is probe traffic and is not read (the analogue of Hotel's token rule, v1 TOKEN_FILTER, which drops every untokened entry-rooted trace); other untokened traces (TeaStore's redirected home page, background work) are read and carry no token
parameters.RESOLUTION_RULE: min positive difference between two distinct values of one instrument inside one fault-free segment (one stream, one cell's fault-free time), minimum over the segments of the fit; for ledger latency (end - start of two float stamps) this is a float-difference granularity, not an instrument resolution, and never binding
parameters.ROUTE_GRAPH_RULE: the call graph for the spike path filter and the BC rules is the project map's (research/project-map/project_map.json callGraph, dt.call_graph), as for Hotel; for TeaStore and OTel its edges and on-route set are restricted to the system's ROUTE_SERVICES_<SYSTEM>, because their project-map base runs drove another route (TeaStore login-browse, OTel the home page with recommendations); Hotel's base run drove the sweep route, so Hotel is not restricted
parameters.SCALE_NOT_ESTIMABLE_RULE: a sensor (incl. a ledger route's latency) with >= MIN_BASELINE_POOLED pooled fault-free points and MAD = 0 in the fit used is 'scale not estimable': its level rules (spike, run3, median) give —, no catch and no false alarm, and it is listed; appear and absent are kept; no quantile threshold
parameters.SENSOR_ABSENT_TOKEN_RULE: a sensor's `absent` catch carries the token(s) of the observation that ends its silence (the stream's first record after the gap): its own token where it carries one (span: the token on the span itself, i.e. the tokened entry root; log: tokens named in the line), else the token(s) of the trace it belongs to (span: the trace's entry-root token, as the harness correlates it; log: the trace the line names, where the cell format carries one); if that request is the ledger's catching request the pair is same-request (H3 c, no win); with neither (no observation ends the silence, or the ending one carries no token and belongs to no tokened trace) the pair is unclassifiable: no win, counted and reported per rate
parameters.SILENCE_START_TOKEN_RULE: an `absent`-vs-`absent` pair (a sensor's `absent` against the ledger's `absent`) is same-request (H3 c, no win) if the silence-STARTING records share a request token OR the silence-ENDING records do (decision 57's test, unchanged). The starting record is the last observation before the silence on each channel: the ledger's last completion before its silence (its tokens), the sensor's last observation before its silence (its own token, else its trace's entry-root token, as decision 57). A pair with a token missing on either start, not already same-request, is unclassifiable (no win, counted). Mixed pairs (only one side `absent`) keep decision 57 / 51. Every absent-vs-absent lead is reported with its decomposition: (ledger's last completion - sensor's last observation, each from the onset in its own clock) + (g_ledger - g_sensor) + residual (clipping at the onset, a whole-second log stamp, a catch moved out of a probe window).
parameters.START_TERM_RULE: an `absent`-vs-`absent` pair that decisions 57 and 58 leave neither same-request nor unclassifiable (different requests start and end the two silences) is a win only if its START term (the ledger's last completion before its silence - the sensor's last observation before its silence, each from the onset in its own clock, i.e. on the common clock through the cell's alignment) exceeds the tie margin (MARGIN_RULE; on the availability clock its availability margin); the gap term (g_ledger - g_sensor) never counts toward a lead and stays printed in the decomposition; a pair whose start term cannot be computed is no win; category 'start term within the margin (decision 60)'. Mixed pairs (only one side `absent`) are unchanged.

parametersV3.V3_APPEAR_RULE: `appear` unchanged (fires on a stream with no record in the fault-free data of the fit); per (sensor, appear) its held-out count is the number of held-out no-fault cells in which the stream appears while having no record in that fold's fit; above the criterion it is dropped. A stream with a record in the pooled scoring fit cannot fire `appear` in an episode and is unarmed for `appear` (unless dropped). Because a stream that can fire `appear` in an episode has no no-fault record, its held-out count is 0 by construction; the held-out `appear` alarms per service (new templates or operations in no-fault time) are reported beside, as the vocabulary-level rate. Sensors whose only calibrated rule is `appear` are listed apart from the other placeable sensors (decision 67).
parametersV3.V3_CALIBRATION_SCOPE_RULE: calibration is per rate and independent of the fault class: a held-out fold is one no-fault cell of the rate scored with v2.4's leave-one-cell-out fit (every valid cell of the rate except that cell, fault cells contributing their pre-onset segment, H1); every armed (sensor, rule) is counted on its own fires, with the detector restarted after each alarm (v2.4's restart semantics restricted to that rule). The episodes are scored with the pooled fit (H1) at each rule's calibrated value. Decision 55's scored-set calibration (M3) is not applied: the unit is the rule, and the class's path filter and by-construction flags still decide which fires count in scoring.

parametersV3.V3_LEDGER_RULE: the ledger E (per route): `failed` is exempt from calibration (the client's definition of failure, the positive control of P1/P2) and always armed; its count in the no-fault cells of each rate is reported. E's `spike`, `run3`, `median` (ok latency) and `absent` (completions) are calibrated like any sensor's rules.
parametersV3.V3_LEVEL_GRID_RULE: level rules (spike, run3, median; the ledger's on ok latency) try K_GRID in ascending order (K <= 100, decision 55, threshold max(K x MAD_SCALE x MAD, relative floor, resolution) as v2.4), then the range fallback (V3_RANGE_FALLBACK_RULE); the first value with at most the criterion's held-out alarms is the rule's calibrated value; none: the rule is dropped. Each rule is calibrated on its own (its own threshold), so run3 and median may fire before spike.
parametersV3.V3_NESTED_RULE: honest nested leave-one-cell-out count of a (sensor, rule) at a rate: for each no-fault cell X of the rate, the grid value is re-selected by the same criterion on the other no-fault cells Y, each scored with a fit that excludes both X and Y (every valid cell of the rate except X and Y, H1); X is then scored at that value with its own leave-one-cell-out fit (exact count, restarted after each alarm). Where no value meets the criterion without X, the rule is not in X's detector (0). Summed over X: the honest count; / T: the honest rate, with its exact bound. A sensor's honest count is the union of its rules so re-selected, simulated per X; a sensor set's likewise (V3_PLACEMENT_FAR_RULE). The honest per-sensor rate is the sensor's false-alarm cost for CELF. F2: the honest count and its hours run over the held-out cells where the rule was in the detector and armed in that cell's fit (`foldsEvaluated`, `honestHours`; the rate's whole T beside); with no such cell the count is — (not evaluable), and a sensor (or set) with no evaluated cell has CELF cost —, never 0.
parametersV3.V3_OPTIMISTIC_ARM_RULE: the optimistic P4 arm scores the episodes with the calibrated detector plus every dropped (sensor, rule) armed at the largest grid value: level rules at K = the last K_GRID value (100), `absent` at the last V3_ABSENT_M_GRID value (5); inert and unarmed rules stay out. It is a bound beside the calibrated arm, never the primary. Printed as 'optimistic bound (not evidence)', never in bold.
parametersV3.V3_P4_RULE: P4 compares the ledger with the placeable sensors in two arms: calibrated (primary: candidates = fires of calibrated rules only) and optimistic (beside: dropped rules also armed at the largest grid value, K = 100 for level rules, m = 5 for `absent`), as H6's pessimistic and optimistic bounds; decision 55's B1 does not apply. Each (class, rate) names the dropped (sensor, rule) pairs and the non-placeable sensors on the class's affected path. The ledger is the OR of its calibrated rules (decision 70, V3_P4_LEDGER_READING); a dropped ledger rule is listed per rate, not a reason for —. P4 is — where fewer episodes than declared exist (as v2.4). The ledger's `failed` is exempt from calibration, always compared, and labelled so in the readout.
parametersV3.V3_PLACEMENT_FAR_RULE: placement-level false alarms of a sensor set at a rate: the honest nested union (V3_NESTED_RULE) of its sensors' rules on the rate's no-fault cells: for each held-out cell, the rules at the values re-selected without that cell, simulated together on it with its leave-one-cell-out fit, the union detector restarted after each alarm; count, hours, rate and the exact one-sided FAR_CONFIDENCE Poisson bound; the sum of the members' counts beside (no independence assumed). On validation cells (campaign B): the calibrated values with the pooled fit. No constraint inside the objective. Only held-out cells where at least one of the set's rules is in the detector and armed count, alarms and hours alike; with none the count is —.
parametersV3.V3_POOL_KEY_RULE: a cell's identity in a pooled run is (its campaign directory, its path inside it); a cell given twice stops the run. Quiet run A2 repeats A's plan and run IDs under a new campaign (decision 68), so a run ID or run path alone is not an identity.
parametersV3.V3_RANGE_FALLBACK_RULE: range fallback of a level rule: lower = min - V3_RANGE_WIDEN_STEPS x resolution, upper = max + V3_RANGE_WIDEN_STEPS x resolution, min/max over the pooled fault-free level values of the fit's cells (the same probe-excluded segment values the median and MAD come from), resolution = the instrument resolution of RESOLUTION_RULE (0 if none). Thresholds per direction: upper - median (up), median - lower (down), compared with dt.beyond (inclusive), so a value one resolution step beyond the fit range fires. Two-sided for metrics, up-only for the latency channels (span durations, ledger latency). Decision 52 kept: a sensor whose fault-free MAD is 0 has no K rule, and the range fallback may apply to it (it needs the median and n >= MIN_BASELINE_POOLED only). Labelled 'range fallback (discrete in effect)': a continuous series always leaves held-out alarms, so in effect it rescues discrete series only. Not tried in the <= 1 alarm sensitivity setting. A range with no instrument resolution in the fit (a constant instrument, e.g. Hotel's sys_io, sys_psi_io, sys_psi_memory at 0.0 everywhere) or a threshold <= 0 is degenerate: the rule is unarmed with the reason 'range degenerate: no instrument resolution in the fit', never a value, never re-armed in the optimistic arm.
parametersV3.V3_STATUS_RULE: each (sensor, rule) at a rate is: calibrated (armed in scoring, held-out count within the criterion at its value, and able to fire inside the hold), dropped (armed, no grid value within the criterion; listed with its held-out count at the last grid value), inert (calibrated by the criterion but unable to fire inside the hold: an `absent` whose scoring gap g exceeds the shortest fault hold of the system; neither calibrated nor a reason to call the sensor placeable), unarmed (cannot fire in scoring at this rate: no pooled level data, pooled n < MIN_BASELINE_POOLED, for K values MAD = 0, for `appear` a record in the pooled fit; listed with the reason) or exempt (the ledger's `failed`). Placeability is per (sensor, rule): a rule is placeable iff calibrated; a sensor with no calibrated rule is 'not placeable at this quiet time'. A K = 100 selection is flagged 'at grid edge'.
parametersV3.V3_TESTABLE_RULE: a held-out fold whose fit cannot arm a (sensor, rule) (level: no pooled scale, n < MIN_BASELINE_POOLED, MAD = 0 for K, a degenerate range; absent: n < MIN_BASELINE_POOLED; appear: a record in the fold's fit) is no evidence: it adds no alarm and no test. A grid value needs at least one armed fold; a rule with no testable value is unarmed ('not testable'). The same holds in the nested re-selection. A rule calibrated on the leave-one-cell-out folds may still be out of the detector, or unarmed, in every nested fold (OTel: 411-460 calibrated rules per rate armed with one cell left out but not with two): its honest count is then — (no nested evidence), never 0 (V3_NESTED_RULE).
parametersV3.V3_VALIDATION_RULE: out-of-sample check: no-fault cells given with --validation are never pooled into a fit or a calibration; each calibrated (sensor, rule) of the rate, each placeable sensor (OR of its rules) and each reported sensor set (union) is run on them with the pooled scoring fit of the main cells, without refitting; counts, hours and the exact bound are reported. Fault cells given as validation are listed and not used.

A lane's cell reads `—` (JSON null) when no sensor of the lane was collected in the cell (`collectedSensors` 0) and 0 fires when sensors were collected and none fired; the summary counts episodes with a fire over episodes with collected sensors, never over all episodes. Beside the counted fire, each lane carries the earliest fire dropped ONLY by a BC flag (`earliestByConstruction`, with `bcFlags`, label 'by construction, not counted'); counting, placement and the pass rule are unchanged.
